question.problem:
Fill in the blanks to make the following reasoning true.

Since $\text{gcd}(22,75)=$
{{field-1}}, 
by the extended Euclidean algorithm, we have 

| $1\,=\,22\,\cdot ($
{{field-2}}
$)+\,75\,\cdot ($
{{field-3}}
$).$ |
| --- |

Therefore, ${22}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,75=$
{{field-4}} (expressed as the smallest nonnegative residue).
question.worked_solution:
First of all, notice that $\text{gcd}(75,22)=1.$ So, the multiplicative inverse of $22$ modulo $75$ exists.

The multiplicative inverse of $22$ modulo $75$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
22\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,75).
$$

To find the value of $x,$ we will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}75 & = & 22\cdot 3 & + & 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 22 & = & 9\cdot 2 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 4\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =75-22\cdot 3 \\ 4 & =22-9\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =9-4\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =9-4\cdot 2 \\  & =9-(22-9\cdot 2)\cdot 2 \\  & =9-22\cdot 2+9\cdot 4 \\  & =9\cdot 5-22\cdot 2 \\  & =(75-22\cdot 3)\cdot 5-22\cdot 2 \\  & =75\cdot 5-22\cdot 15-22\cdot 2 \\  & =75\cdot 5-22\cdot 17 \\  & =22\cdot (-17)+75\cdot (5)\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result modulo $75,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}22\cdot (-17)+75\cdot 5 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,75) \\ 22\cdot (-17) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,75) \\ 22\cdot (75-17) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,75) \\ 22\cdot 58 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,75)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $22\cdot 58≡1\,(\text{mod}\,75),$ which means that ${22}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,75=58.$
